test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: In human beings, excretory products in the form of soluble nitrogen compounds are removed by the ______ in the kidneys.
solution:
The correct answer is __**nephrons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nephrons** are the **microscopic structural and functional units** of the **kidneys**. Each human kidney contains approximately **1 million** to **1.2 million** nephrons.
 
• The primary role of the **nephron** is to process **blood** to remove **metabolic waste** and perform **osmoregulation**.
 
• It filters out **soluble nitrogenous compounds**, primarily **urea**, along with excess **salts** and **water** from the bloodstream to form **urine**.
 
• The filtration process begins in the **Glomerulus**, a high-pressure capillary bed, where **fluid** is pushed into the **Bowman's capsule**.
 
• As the filtrate moves through the **renal tubule**, essential substances like **glucose**, **amino acids**, and **electrolytes** are selectively reabsorbed back into the **blood**.
 
• The remaining concentrated fluid, containing **waste products**, is then collected as **urine** and moved toward the **renal pelvis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Urethra:**

 
 
• The **urethra** is a muscular tube that conveys **urine** from the **urinary bladder** to the outside of the body.
 
• Unlike the **nephron**, it does not perform **filtration** or **waste removal** from the blood; it strictly serves as an **excretory passage**.
 
 
 
• **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate):**
 
 
• **ATP** is known as the **energy currency** of the cell. It is a **nucleotide** that stores and transfers **chemical energy** within cells for metabolism.
 
• While **ATP** provides the energy required for **active transport** in the **kidney tubules**, it is not a physical structure involved in filtering **nitrogenous waste**.
 
 
 
• **Xylem:**
 
 
• **Xylem** is a specialized **vascular tissue** found in **plants**, not in humans.
 
• Its primary function is the **conduction of water** and **dissolved minerals** from the **roots** to the rest of the plant.
 
• It also provides **mechanical support** to the plant structure through **lignified** cell walls.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogenous Wastes in Humans:**
 
 
• Humans are **ureotelic** organisms, meaning we primarily excrete **nitrogen** in the form of **urea**.
 
• **Urea** is produced in the **liver** through the **ornithine cycle** (urea cycle) as a less toxic alternative to **ammonia**.
 
• Efficient removal of these **solutes** is vital to prevent **uremia**, a dangerous accumulation of **waste** in the **blood**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kidney Function:** Apart from **excretion**, kidneys regulate **blood pressure** via the **Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS)** and stimulate **red blood cell** production by secreting **erythropoietin**.
 
• **Homeostasis:** The **nephrons** maintain the **acid-base balance** (pH) of the body by secreting **hydrogen ions** and reabsorbing **bicarbonate ions**.
 
• **Ureter vs. Urethra:** It is important to distinguish between the two; **ureters** carry urine from the **kidneys** to the **bladder**, while the **urethra** carries it from the **bladder** to the external environment.
